_comment: The Warda service listings for this host, per /.well-known/warda-service.json. Each entry is signed independently by the key that service is paid at, so one host's services need not share a key and one bad entry does not invalidate the others. A registry checks two things and repeats everything else: that the signature is by the payee named, and that this document was served from the same host as the endpoint it describes. Everything else here is this operator's claim about itself.
_not_listed: This host also sells /digest at 0.04 KAS, paid to 3c693f61fbc35d1fd4dcec2bbbab692be38656e6fd5a4077ee495afcb23535a1 — agent #001. It is absent because a listing is signed by the key the service is paid at, and that key was printed to a terminal on 3 September 2026 and never saved. The service runs, and is paid every morning; it cannot prove it is its own. An absence here is not evidence that a service does not exist.

services.name: Warda demo vendor — one fact
services.description: A paid endpoint that exists so a stranger can make one real payment in five minutes without writing a service first. Quoted by /start. Priced at 0.03 rather than 0.01 because Kaspa charges storage mass for small outputs and there is a floor under micropayments at roughly 0.02 KAS.

services.name: Warda demo vendor — weather
services.description: A fixed weather reading for Athens, sold to demonstrate a metered request an agent can pay for unattended. The data is not the product; the payment is.

services.name: Warda demo vendor — inference
services.description: A fixed model completion, priced at exactly the demo grant's per-payment cap so a buyer can see the covenant refuse the next one. The data is not the product; the limit is.
